clue.text: Southport's recreations

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for south on a compass
ports are harbour towns; the possessive 's is read as a plural ending

explanation.surface: A note on what the Lancashire seaside resort of Southport offers visitors for fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The town name Southport is split into SOUTH, abbreviated to S, and PORT'S, read as PORTS. Southport is a seaside town in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Games and athletic pastimes are forms of leisure activity, so they count as recreations.

clue.text: Tells of fashionable styles

parts.note: something fashionable is said to be in
styles or shapes are forms

explanation.surface: Someone describes the latest trends in clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: To pass on news or knowledge to someone is to tell them it.

clue.text: A tiny sign perhaps that one's not going out…

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters of these words could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A small signal, maybe on a door, showing that someone is staying home tonight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' tells you to rearrange the nine letters of A TINY SIGN; 'that one's' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Remaining at home for the evening is the opposite of going out.

clue.text: …end by getting fish to eat in

indicators.note: eating takes something inside, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Continuing from the previous clue: the stay-at-home evening ends with fish brought in for supper.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis joins this surface to the clue before; 'by getting' only links definition and wordplay, and 'to eat' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To end something is to complete it, bringing it to a close.

clue.text: Turn pale at the Spanish food!

indicators.note: turn means the letters of the word pale are spun into a new order

parts.note: la is a Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Someone goes white at the sight of a Spanish dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like part of the phrase 'turn pale', but it is the anagram signal, making PAEL; LA is Spanish for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paella is a Spanish rice dish, so it is an example of food.

clue.text: Gore's prs negotiating for advancement

indicators.note: negotiating suggests working the letters round into a new deal, an arrangement

explanation.surface: Al Gore's press officers hammer out terms in the hope of moving forward.
explanation.walkthrough: PRS reads as an abbreviation for public relations staff, but here its letters join GORE'S as fodder for the anagram signalled by 'negotiating'.
explanation.definitionFit: Making headway or moving forward is advancement.

clue.text: Wise to buy such a bond?

definitions.text: Wise to buy such a bond?

parts.words: Wise to buy such a bond?
parts.note: Wise reads as sensible; his first name is also that of the machine that picks winning British premium bonds

explanation.surface: Asks whether it would be prudent to invest in a certain savings bond.
explanation.walkthrough: Premium Bonds are a British government savings scheme whose prize numbers are drawn by a machine with the same first name as Ernie Wise, of the comedy double act Morecambe and Wise.
explanation.definitionFit: The random number generator that chooses premium bond prizes shares its name with Morecambe's comedy partner.

clue.text: Disparaged for having advanced to take German city

indicators.note: to take means the first word swallows the second, holding it inside

parts.note: led means went ahead, advanced
Essen is a city in Germany's Ruhr

explanation.surface: Someone is belittled for pushing forward to capture a German city, like a general criticised for overreaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advanced' reads as moving forward in a campaign, but it is the past tense of lead. 'to take' is the container signal; 'for having' links.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage someone is to belittle them, reducing their standing.

clue.text: It may be on top of girl or bottom of horse

definitions.text: It may be on top of girl or bottom of horse

parts.words: It may be on top of girl or bottom of horse
parts.note: a hairstyle tied high at the back of the head resembles the hair that hangs at the rear of a small horse

explanation.surface: A riddle about something found on a girl's head or a horse's rear.
explanation.definitionFit: Gathered hair worn at the crown is named after the tail of a small horse.

clue.text: Hillhead nuclear power station

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, common on Dartmoor
a ness is a headland, as in Scottish place names

explanation.surface: Names a power station at a place called Hillhead.
explanation.walkthrough: Hillhead looks like a place name but splits into HILL and HEAD. Torness is a nuclear power station on the East Lothian coast of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Torness is a specific nuclear plant in Scotland, so it is an example of a nuclear power station.

clue.text: Spacious, like a big hotel?

explanation.surface: Describes a hotel with plenty of space.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is playful: a big hotel is full of rooms, so it could be called room-y.
explanation.definitionFit: Spacious means having ample space; a large hotel has many rooms, the joke sense.

clue.text: It gives the writer added point

definitions.text: It gives the writer added point

parts.words: It gives the writer added point
parts.note: the writer is a pencil, and the added point is a sharper tip, not an extra argument

explanation.surface: Something that lends an author's argument extra force.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that hones a pencil gives its tip a keener edge.

clue.text: An actor exposing thigh

explanation.surface: A performer showing off a leg on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposing' only links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A ham is an overacting performer; ham is also meat from a pig's thigh, and the back of the thigh.

clue.text: The man with an odd hat gets the girl

parts.note: Sam is a man's name, standing for a typical fellow

indicators.note: odd suggests the letters of hat are out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A romantic comedy: a man in a strange hat wins the woman.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking 'The man' as Sam is loose: Sam stands in for any fellow. 'odd' rearranges HAT to THA; 'with' and 'gets' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: Samantha is a female first name, so it identifies a girl.

clue.text: One way to be wise

parts.note: a way is a road, and putting that road word before wise gives a word for being savvy about city life

explanation.surface: A tip on how to become sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: A street is one kind of way or road, and streetwise means shrewd in urban life.

clue.text: Frustrating, achieving object in war-time

indicators.note: in places the war and time letters inside the word for object

parts.note: a thing is an object
war is taken as written, and time gives T, the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: Achieving a goal during wartime was frustrating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'war-time' looks like one word, but it splits into WAR and T, the usual abbreviation for time. 'in' is the container signal; 'achieving' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Thwarting is blocking someone's plans, which is frustrating them.

clue.text: Make smaller platter, holding very little

indicators.note: holding means one word contains the other

parts.note: a platter is a serving dish
mini means very small, very little

explanation.surface: A large plate with only a tiny portion, as if the food had been shrunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' is the container signal: the very little word sits inside the platter word.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish something is to reduce it in size.

clue.text: Where to have dinner without the German?

definitions.text: Where to have dinner without the German?

indicators.note: without means letters are removed from the word dinner

parts.note: der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Asks where to eat when one's German friend can't come.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing DER (German for 'the') from DINNER leaves the answer, a place where you can have dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub or tavern serves meals to guests.

clue.text: New development makes no sense, as Scots say

indicators.note: as Scots say means the Scottish pronunciation of the words is what we hear

parts.note: a Scot might say no sense as nae sense

explanation.surface: A Scot dismisses some new development as nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: In Scots 'no' is 'nae', and 'nae sense' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nascence is the act of coming into being, a beginning or fresh development.

clue.text: Remains after fire has gone out

indicators.note: gone out suggests the word has is out of order, put out of place

explanation.surface: What is left when a blaze has died.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gone out' reads as the fire being extinguished, but it signals rearranging HAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The powdery residue left after burning is what remains after a fire.

clue.text: Natural colour I found in a pod

indicators.note: found in means the letter I is placed inside another word

parts.note: senna pods are used as a laxative, so pod stands for senna
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a natural pigment inside a pod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts I inside SENNA, after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Sienna is an earth pigment, a brownish yellow or red, so it is a natural colour.

clue.text: Hard water

parts.note: hard water usually means water rich in minerals, but here it is water that has literally gone solid

explanation.surface: A domestic term for mineral-laden tap water.
explanation.definitionFit: Frozen water is solid, so literally hard.

clue.text: Silver pins can cause such skin shreds

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
nails are fastening pins

explanation.surface: Silver pins can scratch, leaving torn skin.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnails are hangnails, torn slivers of skin beside a fingernail.

clue.text: Dispute on the river in French marshland

indicators.note: on in an across clue means the dispute word follows the river word

parts.note: the Cam is the river of Cambridge
argue means dispute

explanation.surface: A quarrel on a river in a marshy French region.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'on' means placed after. The Camargue is the Rhône delta marshland in southern France; the Cam is the river through Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Camargue is a named wetland region in southern France, an example of marsh country.

clue.text: Class as kind

parts.note: taken as written
a sort is a kind or type

explanation.surface: Classify something as a type.
explanation.definitionFit: To assort is to arrange into groups, which is to classify.

clue.text: Dominion a politician and I got into before…

indicators.note: got into means the politician and I go inside another word

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
MP, Member of Parliament, is a politician
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician and the speaker took power before someone else did.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got into' is the container signal; 'a' and 'and' are link words. The ellipsis runs the surface on into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A dominion is a realm ruled by one sovereign power, as an empire is.

clue.text: Clan possibly hidden among trees and peaks

indicators.note: hidden among means the shuffled clan letters are tucked inside another word

parts.note: pines are trees

indicators.note: possibly suggests the letters of clan may be rearranged

explanation.surface: A Scottish clan concealed in a forest among the mountains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CLAN to NACL, and 'hidden among' is the container signal, though it looks like the hidden-word kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinnacles are pointed summits, so they are peaks.

clue.text: …to retrospectively check government involvement in Africa

indicators.note: involvement means the government letter is wrapped up inside the turned word
retrospectively means looking back, so the word for check is read backwards

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: a look back at checking the state's role in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retrospectively' turns REIN into NIER, and 'involvement' puts G inside it. The definition is loose: the answer is a country in Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Niger is a landlocked country in West Africa, so it is located in that continent.

clue.text: Rover taking public transport to Portugal

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport
P is the international vehicle registration code for Portugal

explanation.surface: A wanderer catches a tram heading to Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a vagrant who wanders, a rover.

clue.text: Chanting at last orders for two gin cocktails!

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word orders
cocktails are mixtures, so the letters are mixed up
two means the word gin is used twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Raucous chanting as a pub calls last orders for two gin cocktails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'two' doubles GIN to GINGIN, 'at last' gives S from orders, and 'cocktails' mixes the seven letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Chanting is a form of vocal music, so it is singing.

clue.text: Cambridge student working as cowboy

explanation.surface: A Cambridge undergraduate has a job herding cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: At Cambridge a wrangler is a student gaining first-class honours in mathematics; 'working as' links the two definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: A top Cambridge maths graduate has this title; it is also a ranch hand handling horses.

clue.text: Make an attack on cleaner, for example, returning

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady

indicators.note: returning means the abbreviation for for example comes back reversed

explanation.surface: Someone launches an assault on a cleaner who is coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns EG into GE. A char, or charwoman, is British for a cleaner; 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To charge is to rush forward in an assault, making an attack.
